title: Apps and Public Wi-Fi
about: Choose what apps can use, and stay safe on public Wi-Fi.

cards.prompt: A torch app asks to see your contacts. It needs them to work.
cards.explanation: False. A torch only needs your phone's light. Asking for contacts is more than its job needs.
cards.hint: What does a torch app actually do?
cards.nudge: Think about the torch's one job. Do contacts help with it?

cards.sentence: An **app permission** lets an app use your camera, microphone, location or contacts.

cards.prompt: Does the app **need** it for its job?
cards.explanation: Allow what fits the app's job, like location for maps or the microphone for calls. A torch app needs your light, not who your aunt is.
cards.hint: For each one, ask: could the app do its main job without it?
cards.nudge: Think about what each app is for. A permission unrelated to that job isn't needed.

cards.sentence: For location, choose **"Only while using the app"**, so a closed app can't see where you are.

cards.prompt: You install a new drawing game.

steps.text: It asks: **"Allow access to your contacts?"** then **"Allow location: Always?"** What do you do?

choices.text: Allow both, so the game works
choices.consequence: A drawing game doesn't need your contacts or where you are, all the time.

choices.text: Say no to both, and see if the game still works
choices.consequence: It does. You can always change it later in Settings if a feature really needs it.

cards.explanation: Say no to permissions an app doesn't need. If it **won't work at all** without ones unrelated to its job, choose a different app.
cards.hint: Would a drawing game need your contacts, or your location all the time?

cards.prompt: You can switch an app's permission off later in Settings.
cards.explanation: True. Any permission can be turned off in **Settings**, so you can change your mind any time.
cards.hint: Where on your phone do you control what apps can use?
cards.nudge: Permissions aren't for ever: look in your phone's Settings.

cards.prompt: Which gives a weather app your location, **and no more**?

options.text: Only while using: when you open it

options.nudge: The forecast only matters when you look. Does it need to know where you go while it's closed?
A local forecast does use where you are. The question is how much of the time.

cards.explanation: **"Only while using the app"** shares your location when you check, not while it's closed. "Always" is more than it needs. ("Never" works too if you type your town in.)
cards.hint: When do you actually need the forecast for where you are?

cards.sentence: **Public Wi-Fi** in cafés and shops is shared, and you can't always be sure it's real.

cards.prompt: Fine on public Wi-Fi, or better on **mobile data**?
cards.explanation: Everyday browsing is fine on public Wi-Fi. For money or important accounts, **mobile data** is safer, since you can't always be sure a network is real.
cards.hint: Which ones involve your money or your most important accounts?
cards.nudge: Ask of each one again: does it involve money or an important account?

cards.prompt: Check your bank on ___, not on public Wi-Fi.

options.nudge: Café Wi-Fi is public Wi-Fi, and you can't always be sure it's the real one.
Free networks are exactly the ones you can't be sure about.

cards.explanation: **Mobile data** goes straight to your phone company, so it's safer for money and important accounts.
cards.hint: Which connection isn't shared with strangers?

cards.prompt: At a café, which is **riskiest**? (A **fake hotspot** is Wi-Fi named to look like the café's.)

options.text: Join "Free Cafe WiFi 2" when staff don't know it
Read the news on the network staff told you about
options.nudge: The café's real network is fine for news. Which choice could hand your details to a stranger?

options.text: Check your bank account on mobile data, not Wi-Fi
options.nudge: Mobile data is the safer choice for banking. Which network can nobody vouch for?

cards.explanation: Staff have never heard of "Free Cafe WiFi 2", so it might be a **fake hotspot**. Ask staff for the real name, and turn off auto-join for public networks.
cards.hint: Which network could belong to a stranger instead of the café?

cards.prompt: A **microphone dot** appears while you're reading. (It means an app is using the mic.)

steps.text: You're not on a call. What do you do?

choices.text: Check which app; switch its mic off
choices.consequence: Your phone shows which app it is. You turn its microphone permission off in Settings.
The dot means an app is listening right now. It's worth a quick check.
The dot may go for now, but the app still has permission and could listen again later.

cards.explanation: The dot shows an app is using the **microphone**. Find out which app, and switch that permission off if it doesn't need it.
cards.hint: The dot means some app is using the microphone. Where can you stop an app using it for good?

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Give apps only the **permissions** they need; choose **"Only while using"** for location.
- On **public Wi-Fi**, check the name, and bank on **mobile data**.
- **Try this:** switch one app's location to "Only while using".
